title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic ships the governance layer — Enterprise admin analytics + model-level entitlements + spend alerts, a FedRAMP-High Claude for Government desktop, and Claude Desktop for Linux
bullets.summary: The Enterprise admin dashboard now breaks usage/cost down by group and user (artifacts, files edited, skills/connectors shown next to cost); model-level entitlements + spend alerts meter which models run where; Claude Code + Cowork land in a FedRAMP-High government desktop with tamper-evident audit logs and local history; and Claude Desktop hits Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+, x86_64 + arm64).
bullets.how: This is the observability + cost-governance the Construct fleet has lacked — per-agent, per-skill, per-connector spend, plus model gating by entitlement. The tamper-evident audit-log + local-history pattern is the compliance story PRAGMA sells to regulated operators, and Linux desktop lets us run the same harness on cheap server hardware, not just the Mac.

bullets.title: Press Ranger ships the first MCP server for press-release distribution — PR becomes an agent-callable workflow
bullets.summary: The V1 server connects Claude, ChatGPT, and OpenAI Codex directly to Press Ranger so an AI conversation becomes a complete PR workflow: draft, target the media list, and distribute without leaving the agent.
bullets.how: Direct fit for Pulse's owned-presence remit and Brand 9 Signs earned media: one Construct agent that drafts in brand voice and pushes a release to targeted outlets. Bank it as a candidate owned-presence MCP behind Pulse; the SaaS-replacement wedge is real, but vet media-list quality before trusting distribution.

bullets.title: arXiv: In-Context Prompting Obsoletes Agent Orchestration for Procedural Tasks
bullets.summary: For procedural tasks, putting the entire procedure in the system prompt and letting the model self-orchestrate dominates orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK), which add coordination overhead without accuracy gains.
bullets.how: A counterweight to over-building the harness: for well-specified procedural jobs (a fixed scan-and-write pipeline like this one) our CLAUDE.md-in-the-prompt approach is likely already optimal. Reserve multi-agent orchestration for open-ended work; keep procedural agents as a single well-specified prompt with verification.

bullets.title: Frontier shuffle — Gemini 3.5 Pro rebuilt from scratch and slipped to Jul 17 with a 2M-token window; Apple sues OpenAI over trade secrets
bullets.summary: Google scrapped the 2.5 Pro architecture for a full pretraining rebuild (math reasoning, SVG, image quality), now shipping ~Jul 17 with a 2M-token context and Deep Think gated behind a $250/mo Ultra tier; separately, on Jul 11 Apple sued OpenAI for trade-secret theft citing 400+ ex-Apple staff now at OpenAI.
bullets.how: The 2M-token window is worth testing for whole-corpus jobs (Harvard library, full brand-context passes) once GA. Treat model churn as swappable config behind provider-agnostic routing and don't re-tool around any single vendor while the field reshuffles and litigates.

bullets.title: Agent funding rewards the agent-runs-its-own-raise story — Lyzr $100M Series B, Bespoke Labs $40M Series A, Taktile $110M Series C
bullets.summary: Lyzr (enterprise agents) raised a $100M Series B at ~$500M by letting its own agent run the round; Bespoke Labs took $40M Series A for safe environments where agents learn before production; Taktile pulled $110M Series C for an agentic decision platform for banks and insurers.
bullets.how: Signal, not a tool: capital is funding agent training/eval environments (Bespoke) and governed decision platforms (Taktile) — the harness and safety layer, not one-off app agents. Reinforces the thesis: durable edge is owned orchestration, memory, and a real reviewer/verification step; Lyzr's agent-run raise is a proof point to show clients.

praxis_lesson: The afternoon's real story is governance graduating onto the platform — per-user/per-skill/per-connector cost analytics, model-level entitlements, spend alerts, tamper-evident audit logs, and a Linux desktop mean the Construct fleet can now be metered, gated, and run on cheap hardware, and the FedRAMP-grade audit posture is itself the PRAGMA sales story. Meanwhile the research (in-context prompting beating orchestration for procedural tasks) says don't over-build: keep procedural agents as one well-specified prompt + verification, reserve orchestration for open-ended work, wire vertical MCPs like Press Ranger behind Pulse instead of hand-rolling, and treat frontier-model churn (Gemini 3.5 Pro's rebuild, Apple v. OpenAI) as swappable config behind provider-agnostic routing.
